title: Copy a Google Sheets tab to another file with AI
nav: copy a tab to another spreadsheet
h1: copy one google sheets tab into another spreadsheet
description: Move a copy of one Google Sheets tab into an existing spreadsheet with a bot. Identify the source tab and destination file before creating the duplicate.
keyword: copy google sheets tab with ai
keywords: chatgpt copy sheet to another spreadsheet
ai copy tab between google spreadsheets
answer:
**give the meeting its briefing tab without handing over the whole workbook.** the bot copies one google sheets tab into an existing destination spreadsheet. give it both file links, the direction and the tab name.

the original stays put. the copy is a snapshot, so later source edits won't follow.
og_line: the briefing tab goes where you need it.
what:
**hand over the useful tab without sending the whole workbook.** the bot finds the tab from its name and copies it into the destination file. say which link is the source and which is the destination.

the destination must already exist. this action can't choose a new tab name or copy just a few cells. those need separate steps. it's a snapshot: later edits to the source won't follow.
uses: **put the agenda where the meeting happens.** copy its prepared tab into the existing meeting workbook.
**start a project from an agreed plan.** copy the planning tab from your template file.
**hand over one report.** add the selected reporting tab to the review workbook.
**experiment away from the original.** copy the worksheet into a separate analysis file.

routine.message:
every other wednesday at 15:10, find this fortnight's dated briefing tab in the research workbook. look in the steering workbook for an existing copy of that briefing.

if a copy exists, stop and tell me. otherwise show both file names and the dated tab here. ask me before copying the complete tab. never copy other tabs or rename anything.
routine.needs: google sheets read and write; access to the source and permission to add a destination tab
routine.output:
copy proposal

- source: ivo marsh's research workbook, this fortnight's briefing tab
- destination: willow bend steering
- scope: one complete tab

ready for you to approve this direction.

steps: **connect both files.** the bot needs google sheets read and write, plus access to source and destination.
**give both links.** say which direction to copy and name the tab.
**read the proposal.** require your yes before it adds the tab.
**inspect the first copy.** keep the routine only for fresh dated briefings. pause after a one-time handoff.
watch: **similar tab names are easy to mix up.** use the exact one you want.
**the whole tab goes across.** this action has no cell selection. choose another approach for an excerpt.
**a retry can create another copy.** inspect the destination after a timeout before trying again.
**copies grow apart.** later source edits do not update the destination. decide separately whether to copy again.

faq.q: does it copy the whole spreadsheet?
faq.a: **no, just one tab.** the other tabs stay in the source file.

faq.q: can it make a new destination spreadsheet too?
faq.a: **make that file first.** use **create a google sheet**, then give the new file link as the destination.

faq.q: can i choose the new tab name in the same request?
faq.a: **this copy action cannot name it.** renaming needs another allowed action.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

steps: open the source and destination spreadsheets
copy their links to the bot
name one tab and ask for a copy proposal
confirm the copy goes from source to destination

mistakes.mistake: expecting the copy to stay current
mistakes.fix: treat it as a snapshot. later source edits need a separate update.

mistakes.mistake: retrying when the reply is unclear
mistakes.fix: look in the destination first. the tab may already be there.

items: the source tab is the right dated briefing
the whole tab belongs in that destination
there is no existing copy of this briefing

tip.text: two links don't say which way the copy goes.
